structured_output.statement: Worked example, Section 2.3 "Position vs. Time Graphs", p. 85: "Find the average velocity of the car whose position is graphed in Figure 1.13." The strategy given is that the slope of a d-vs-t graph is the average velocity (rise over run); the solution picks the two labelled points (6.4 s, 2000 m) and (0.50 s, 525 m) and substitutes them into equation 2.8.
structured_output.notes:
Rule 4 governs. The computation asked for is the slope of a position-time graph — a velocity obtained as Δd/Δt from two graph points. engineering.mechanics registers no slope type. mechanics.uniform-motion runs the other way (it produces a displacement from a given speed and duration); the passage gives no speed as a given and asks for one as the result, so mapping it onto uniform-motion would mean inverting the registered relation and treating the sought quantity as an input. That is bending it into the nearest type, which rule 4 forbids. The two point coordinates are stated as given, but they are graph readings feeding a slope, not a speed-and-time pair.

A second, independent blocker also applies. The solution's result lives in equation 2.8, which the text layer carries as a bare equation number with no value — the passage asserts no readable velocity in the Solution. The Discussion mentions "900 km/h, or about 560 mi/h", but those are a parenthetical restatement in non-SI units inside commentary, one of them explicitly approximate ("about"), and neither is the m/s figure the worked example computed; the other m/s numbers in the Discussion (27 m/s, 343 m/s, 15 m/s) belong to the highway limit, the land-speed record, and a different subsequent motion, not to this result. So rule 2 would also fail here (no_readable_result) had the type gate passed. Only one reason can be reported; the type gate is the prior one, since the problem could not be recomputed by the kernel even with a readable answer.

Note also that the prose says Figure 1.13 while the later Discussion refers to Figure 2.13 for a different graph; this discrepancy is reproduced as the document carries it and is not corrected. No physics has been checked or corrected.
